**ANTHONY, 2026-08-14: "always trying to improve the probability that an agent uses a reflow2 skill or tool — we can probably look at the stats." MEASURED ACROSS EVERY RETAINED TRANSCRIPT. TWO FINDINGS: THE TREND IS ALREADY STEEPLY UP, AND THE INSTRUMENT THAT WOULD TELL HIM SO UNDERCOUNTS BY A THIRD.**

═══ ⭐⭐ THE TREND, BY WEEK (get_skill channel, sessions with ≥1 reflow2 call) ═══
```
week         sessions   with-skill   rate
2026-07-13       4          0         0%
2026-07-20      16          1         6%
2026-07-27      22         14        64%
2026-08-03      15         15       100%
2026-08-10       6          5        83%   <- 5 of 6; the one miss is THIS session
```
**The headline aggregate (35 of 63 = 56%) is an artefact of averaging over the era before the fix.** On current behaviour the rate is 83–100%. ⚠️ The last two buckets are small (15 and 6 sessions) and the trend is not proof of causation — nothing here isolates WHICH change moved it.

═══ 🛑 THE INSTRUMENT MEASURES ONE OF TWO CHANNELS ═══

`surface_usage.py` counts skill use as **`get_skill` calls**. In the reflow2 checkout a skill is far more often invoked as a **slash command** — Claude Code loads `.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md` as `/<name>`, and that path never touches `get_skill`. Counting only invocation markers (`<command-name>`, the Skill tool's base-directory line), never mere mentions of a path:
```
sessions with >=1 reflow2 call         63
  get_skill  (what the instrument sees) 35   56%
  slash-command / Skill invocation      55   87%
  EITHER                                60   95%
  invoked a skill, counted as ZERO      25
```
⇒ **25 sessions used a skill and register as total failures.** `where-am-i` is the clearest case: **37 local invocations against 4 `get_skill` calls**, because `/where` is one of the shipped commands.

⚠️ A FIRST ATTEMPT AT THIS MEASUREMENT WAS WRONG AND IS RECORDED AS SUCH: matching `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` anywhere in a transcript reported 90%, because it also matched `ls` output, greps of the skill tree, and the SessionStart hook's own catalogue. **Mentions are not invocations.** The numbers above use invocation markers only.

═══ ⭐⭐ WHY THE BIAS IS THE SAME BLIND SPOT FOUND TWICE ALREADY TODAY ═══

The local channel **exists only where the skill files do** — the reflow2 checkout, which holds all twenty as the compile sources. A CONSUMER INSTALL HAS NEITHER THE SOURCES NOR MOST COMMANDS, so `get_skill` really is their only channel and the instrument is correct for them. **It is wrong precisely and only for the maintainer's own sessions**, which are the ones he reads.

This is the third instance in one day of one structural fault: `fact:the-commands-cover-nine-of-twenty-skills-and-the-checkout-cannot-feel-it` (the checkout resolves all 20 as commands, a consumer resolves 9) and `fact:updating-reflow2-does-not-update-a-project-already-set-up` (the developer's kit is a SYMLINK, a consumer's is a frozen tarball). **`req:the-tool-finds-its-own-blind-spots` keeps arriving in the ENVIRONMENT rather than in a detector.**

→ AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS ON `dec:idea-does-every-served-skill-get-a-command`: a skill WITH a command is invoked locally and vanishes from `get_skill`; a skill WITHOUT one can arrive by no other route. **The eleven uncovered skills are the only ones the instrument can see honestly.**

═══ 🛑 TWO SKILLS HAVE NEVER BEEN INVOKED BY EITHER CHANNEL, IN ANY RETAINED SESSION ═══

**`ingest-corpus` and `link-projects`** — zero `get_skill`, zero invocations. link-projects was WRITTEN 2026-08-13 (PR #169) to make the linking process reusable, and the process has not been run through it since. A skill nobody reaches for is not evidence it is unneeded, but it is the sharpest case `dec:bl-155` describes: reflow2 cannot tell UNUSED from UNREACHABLE.

═══ THE SESSION THAT PRODUCED THIS MEASUREMENT IS THE ONE MISS ═══

🛑 Session `809c87ed`, 2026-08-14: 43 reflow2 calls, **zero `get_skill`**. It invoked `/capture-session` locally — so the instrument's verdict is wrong in MECHANISM — **and it is right in SUBSTANCE anyway: building the decomposition detector, `impact-check` was never opened before changing an existing design, and the Stop hook had to point out that `propagate_change` had been skipped.** Recorded rather than argued away: the honest reading is that one skill was used where two or three applied.

═══ SEPARATE SIGNAL WORTH KEEPING: THE SURFACE IS MISSING BULK FORMS ═══

45.3% of tool-to-tool transitions are the SAME tool called again (3474/7671). Worst: `release_includes` 989 self-loops over 1010 calls in 8 sessions (~126 per session) — and `release_includes_all` already exists, so this is a DISCOVERABILITY failure, not a missing feature. Then `set_artifact_checksum` (288/522, 40 sessions), `create_node` (150/393). **Nobody calls one tool 126 times because they want to.**

⇒ 118 of 149 served tools were called at least once; 35 never were. Absence stays WEAK evidence — only retained transcripts are visible, and a tool used before the window looks identical to one never used.
